referralPage.heading: Community Resources
referralPage.intro: Vetted local resources to refer youth and families to: therapy and psychiatric care, suicide safety, basic needs, and community organizations. Search by name, city, or need, and see locations on the map.
referralPage.disclaimer: Compiled by Rise providers. Details change, so call ahead to confirm eligibility, cost, and availability before referring.
referralPage.label: Search community resources
referralPage.placeholder: Name, city, ZIP code, or need (e.g. food, housing, IOP, Spanish)
referralPage.mapEmptyCaption: Pins show resources with a single street address. Multi-location and virtual services appear in the list only.
referralPage.emptyText: Nothing matches that search. Try a different word, or choose All.

sections.label: Therapy & Psychiatric Care
sections.intro: Outpatient therapy, IOP/PHP, inpatient, crisis walk-in, assessment, support groups, and substance use support.

sections.label: Suicide Safety
sections.intro: Suicide prevention, therapy funding, and lethal means safety.

sections.label: Basic Needs
sections.intro: Food, housing, financial assistance, childcare, clothing, and benefits help for students and families.

sections.label: Youth & Family Organizations
sections.intro: Affinity groups, mentoring, family support, and legal and restorative justice organizations.

sections.label: Office Space for Sessions
sections.intro: Free and low-fee rooms for Rise therapists to meet with clients. All vetted by Rise.

items.name: Second Wind Fund
items.description: Matches children and youth at risk of suicide with a licensed therapist and pays for up to 12 therapy sessions when cost or access is a barrier.
items.eligibility: Youth 19 and younger at risk of suicide who face a financial or social barrier to treatment

items.name: Colie's Closet
items.description: Peer education group that goes into classrooms to present warning signs and risk factors, with the goal of educating youth about suicide and depression for prevention. Also provides financial assistance to help youth experiencing depression or suicidal thoughts receive therapy.
items.eligibility: Middle school and high school classes
items.referral: Email coliesclosetboco@gmail.com, or students can fill out the interest form online.

items.name: North Range Behavioral Health: gun locks
items.description: Gun locks.

items.name: Guidelight
items.description: Begins with a psychiatric evaluation and personal assessment; offers medication management and one-on-one and group therapy. IOP: average of 4 weeks, 3 hours a day, 5 days a week. PHP: for people who need intensive care but not 24-hour inpatient support; average of 2 weeks, 6 hours a day, 5 days a week. Includes an LGBTQIA+ inclusive IOP. In person or virtual.
items.address: Central Park, Cherry Creek, Colorado Springs
items.referral: Schedule an admissions appointment online.

items.name: Della Cava Behavioral Health
items.description: Inpatient facility offering safety and stabilization for adults in acute emotional crisis.
items.referral: Call to begin intake.

items.name: Centennial Peaks
items.description: Inpatient care for adults struggling with mental health and substance use disorders.
items.referral: Walk in, call, or fill out the form online.

items.name: North Range Behavioral Health
items.description: Child, youth, and family support; school-based support; family and community-based treatment.
items.payment: Will not deny care based on inability to pay
items.referral: Call or fill out the online form.

items.name: Ardent Grove Foundation
items.description: Affordable trauma-informed therapy and assessment services: individual, couples, and family therapy, EMDR, psychological testing, and eating disorder support groups.
items.address: 1780 S Bellaire St., Suite 500, Denver, CO 80222
items.referral: Fill out the online form.

items.name: Regis Behavioral Health
items.address: Denver Metro (telehealth for all of Colorado)

items.name: Reaching Hope
items.description: Trauma-informed therapy: individual and group, in person and virtual.

items.name: Leaf
items.description: Individual therapy, group therapy, psychoeducational classes, assessment and referral, community-based wellness, youth programming, and suicide education and prevention.

items.name: Denver Children’s Advocacy Center (Denver CAC)
items.description: Child and family therapy, resource coordination, and support groups. No documentation needed; takes Medicaid. Waitlist about 1 month.

items.name: Charlie Health
items.description: Virtual intensive outpatient program.
items.referral: Refer online at https://www.charliehealth.com/referrers or call 866-948-2178.

items.name: Redpoint Center
items.address: Boulder, Longmont, Thornton, Greeley, Fort Collins, Glenwood Springs
items.payment: Most insurance accepted (verify on their website)

items.name: Harmony Recovery
items.address: 1600 Fish Hatchery Rd, Estes Park, CO 80517

items.name: Medicine Horse
items.description: One-on-one and group options available.
items.address: 7663 E. County Line Road North, Longmont, CO 80504

items.name: Ellie Mental Health
items.description: Individual and family therapy, in person and virtual.
items.address: 275 S Main St, Suite 201, Longmont, CO 80501

items.name: Mayamotion Healing
items.description: Culturally competent therapy.
items.cost: $90–$200 per session (50–55 minutes); sliding scale offered

items.name: Sample Therapy Services
items.description: Substance use treatment, DUI support, anxiety, depression, trauma, and family counseling.

items.name: Glass Lawler Mental Health (The Center on Colfax)
items.description: Complimentary mental health services (12 free sessions) and support groups for LGBTQ+ adults.
items.address: The Center on Colfax, 1301 E. Colfax Ave., Denver, CO 80218
items.referral: No referral or insurance required. Referrals to other affirming therapeutic services or community resources are also provided.

items.name: 988 Walk-in Centers
items.description: Walk-in crisis centers connected to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

items.name: AllHealth Network
items.description: Sees children, adolescents, young adults, families and adults. Psychiatric evaluations offered; inpatient and outpatient options.
items.address: 6507 S Santa Fe Dr, Littleton, CO 80120
items.referral: Phone intake counselors are available at all hours to receive referrals from the community, area hospitals, or the AllHealth Network crisis hotline.

items.name: Blue Sky Bridge
items.description: Child advocacy for child abuse and neglect; trauma-focused CBT (TF-CBT) and EMDR for children who have experienced a traumatic event.
items.eligibility: Children ages 4–18 in Boulder County who have had a forensic interview
items.referral: Referral can be made after the forensic interview.

items.name: Antelope Recovery
items.description: Teen IOP for teens experiencing substance use, anxiety, depression, self-harm, suicidal thoughts, trauma, and interpersonal difficulties; parent support programs.
items.referral: Schedule a consultation online.

items.name: Children's Hospital Colorado
items.description: Emergency mental health assessment for children and adolescents experiencing suicidal thoughts, suicide attempts, worsening depression or anxiety, or uncontrollable behavior. Services include evaluating immediate safety, medical stabilization when needed, behavioral health screening, and determining the appropriate level of ongoing care.
items.address: North Campus (Boulder-area option): 469 State Highway 7, Broomfield, CO 80023; Anschutz Medical Campus: 13123 East 16th Avenue, Aurora, CO 80045; South Campus: 1811 Plaza Drive, Highlands Ranch, CO 80129
items.cost: Varies by services and insurance coverage; financial assistance may be available
items.payment: Private insurance, Medicaid/CHP+, and self-pay; payment plans and financial assistance available
items.referral: No referral or appointment needed for emergency mental health evaluations.
items.languages: English and Spanish; free interpreters for other spoken languages and sign language

items.name: Griffith Centers
items.description: Trauma-informed individual and family therapy for anxiety, depression, trauma, grief, and behavioral concerns. In-office, home/community-based, and telehealth options.
items.eligibility: Children, teens, adults, and families in Colorado
items.address: Northglenn: 10190 Bannock St., Suite 120, Northglenn, CO 80260; Centennial: 7955 E. Arapahoe Ct., #3100, Centennial, CO 80112
items.referral: “Make a Referral” form, or schedule a consultation.

items.name: MESA (Moving to End Sexual Assault)
items.description: Emotional support, advocacy, case management, resource referrals, and accompaniment to hospital exams, police interviews, and court. Support groups and wellness programs also available.
items.cost: Hotline and text support are free; some support groups are free; wellness program fees vary
items.referral: Contact MESA directly by phone or email.

items.name: NAMI Boulder County
items.description: Free peer-led support groups, mental health education, family/caregiver classes, and information about local resources.
items.address: 1455 Dixon Ave., Lafayette, CO 80026 (group locations vary; virtual options available)
items.referral: Contact NAMI directly.

items.name: Parent & Family Wellness Center
items.description: Individual, child/teen, couples, and family therapy; psychiatric evaluations and medication management. Specializes in pregnancy/postpartum mental health, reproductive concerns, parenting, trauma, anxiety, and depression. In person and telehealth.

items.name: Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance (DBSA)
items.description: Peer-led support groups, educational resources, and wellness tools for people experiencing depression or bipolar disorder.
items.address: Meeting locations vary; online groups available

items.name: TRU Community Care: Grief Services
items.description: Grief support and resources for people coping with the death of a loved one, including support groups.

items.name: Mindful Works
items.description: A social enterprise offering work to people striving to overcome obstacles due to mental health challenges. Through hands-on craft, people rebuilding their lives gain real skills while making useful products for the Boulder community, and a stronger sense of belonging.
items.referral: Contact them directly.

items.name: Alis Behavioral Health
items.description: Teens and pre-teens receive a customized, comprehensive care plan developed by a multidisciplinary team, the family, and the client, reviewed and revised to match the level of care needed.
items.eligibility: 11–17 years old (18 if still in high school)
items.address: 2921 West 120th Avenue #100, Westminster, CO 80234; 1325 S Colorado Blvd, Suite B705, Denver, CO 80222
items.referral: Contact them directly, or sign up through the referral tab on their website.

items.name: Hopelight
items.description: Primary medical care for all ages, pediatric behavioral health, and counseling/wellness programs, with an on-site pharmacy and laboratory services.

items.name: Conscious Winds Counseling
items.description: Therapy for individuals, couples, and families; trauma- and culturally-informed therapy including EMDR, DBT, CBT, MBCT, PE, CPT, and IFS.
items.address: 1800 30th St. Ste. 308, Boulder, CO 80301; 3955 E. Exposition Ave. Ste. 212, Denver, CO 80209

items.name: Axis Integrated Mental Health
items.description: Psychiatry, therapy, Deep TMS and Spravato treatment.
items.address: 400 S McCaslin Blvd, Suite 111, Louisville, CO 80027; 8758 Wolff Ct., Suite 205, Westminster, CO 80031; 1444 S Potomac St, Suite 220, Aurora, CO 80012; 6950 E Belleview Ave, Suite 300, Denver, CO 80111

items.name: Boulder Emotional Wellness
items.description: Couples and relationship counseling, individual therapy, and play therapy.

items.name: Empowered Play
items.description: A trauma-informed, affirming, strengths-based, and child-led practice: play therapy, teen counseling, parent support, and walking therapy.
items.address: 2130 Mountain View Ave, Longmont, CO 80501; 275 Century Cir. #200, Louisville, CO; 5205 S College Ave Unit B, Fort Collins, CO

items.name: I Matter
items.description: Connects youth 18 and younger (21 and younger for those receiving special education services) with a licensed therapist for up to 6 free counseling sessions.
items.eligibility: Youth 18 and younger (21 and younger with special education services)

items.name: Kidskills Therapy
items.description: Pediatric therapy practice, including occupational therapy.
items.address: Kid Skills Clinic, 9505 Yellowstone Rd, Longmont, CO

items.name: Kidstuff Counseling
items.description: Pediatric counseling, parent counseling, family counseling, and teen counseling.
items.address: Westminster, Aurora, Fort Collins, Greeley, Grand Junction, Longmont, Loveland

items.name: LifeStance Health
items.address: 777 29th St Ste 500, Boulder, CO 80303 (one of many locations)

items.name: Momentum Counseling
items.eligibility: Children, teens, adults, couples, and families

items.name: WellMind (Well Mind Connection)
items.description: A free, bilingual, and confidential mental health and resource navigation hub in Boulder County.

items.name: The Works Program
items.description: Helps people who use drugs reduce their risk of disease and overdose death, and increases access to referrals and supportive services, including HIV, hepatitis C, syphilis, chlamydia, and gonorrhea testing and treatment, substance use recovery, and mental health resources.
items.address: Boulder County AIDS Project (BCAP), 2118 14th Street, Boulder (one of several locations)

items.name: Colorado Healing Collective
items.description: Counseling services provided by master’s-level interns working toward degrees in counseling psychology or social work.

items.name: Full Circle Program
items.description: Age-specific drug and alcohol support groups for teens and young adults in Boulder and surrounding areas, plus groups focused on other high-risk behaviors, and weekly support groups for parents and family members.

items.name: Spectrum Health
items.description: Medication management; autism, anxiety disorders, and BPD.

items.name: Umbrella Collective
items.description: LGBTQIA+ affirming therapy.

items.name: Whole Connection
items.description: Trauma-informed therapy.

items.name: Community Economic Defense Project
items.description: Eviction assistance, foreclosure assistance, utility assistance, resource navigation, and disaster relief.
items.eligibility: Colorado residents in need of housing support
items.address: 1600 N. Downing St., Suite 600, Denver, CO 80218
items.referral: Fill out the form online; the form depends on the support needed.

items.name: OUR Center
items.description: Financial assistance, food and basic needs assistance, support programs, mental and physical health resources, employment resources, and legal support.
items.eligibility: St. Vrain Valley School District residents (proof of at least 60 days of residency)
items.referral: Depends on need: call, text, or use the contact form online; for the market or café, go in person.

items.name: Safehouse Progressive Alliance for Nonviolence
items.description: Safety planning with domestic violence survivors; short-term rental assistance; landlord support and Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) lease breaks; Boulder County Coordinated Entry; Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) applications.
items.eligibility: Adults, youth, and children impacted by domestic or dating violence
items.referral: Call or email hotline@safehousealliance.org.

items.name: TGTHR
items.description: Housing support for youth experiencing homelessness, including 1440 Pine, a 40-unit permanent supportive housing complex in Boulder. Residents receive individualized case management, employment support, education support, access to behavioral healthcare, and leadership opportunities.
items.eligibility: Housing for ages 18–24 experiencing homelessness; resources for ages 12–24
items.address: The Source: 3080 Broadway, Boulder, CO 80304; housing: 1440 Pine St, Boulder, CO
items.referral: Drop in at The Source or call with questions.

items.name: Emergency Family Assistance Association (EFAA)
items.description: Resource navigation, financial assistance, and a food bank.
items.eligibility: City of Boulder and BVSD mountain communities in Boulder County
items.referral: Call to learn more and see if you qualify; fill out the online form for financial assistance. Phone or in-person appointments.

items.name: Community Food Share
items.description: Food banks and food financial assistance; an on-site food pantry and many other locations, including mobile food pantries.
items.eligibility: Boulder County or Broomfield County residents
items.referral: Enroll at https://cfs.waitwell.us/, then reserve an appointment up to a week in advance.

items.name: Harvest of Hope Pantry
items.description: Food pantry.
items.eligibility: Boulder County residents: weekly shopping; non-residents or unhoused: daily shopping
items.referral: Walk in; no appointment needed.

items.name: Sister Carmen Community Center
items.description: Food bank, thrift store, financial assistance, and parenting support.
items.eligibility: Residents of Lafayette, Louisville, Superior, and Erie
items.referral: Call to get connected with an advocate; limited assistance if walk-in through the food bank.

items.name: Colorado WIC
items.description: Free healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and referrals to other care.
items.eligibility: Colorado residents who are pregnant, breastfeeding a baby under 1, had a baby in the past 6 months, or caring for a child under 5. All caregivers can apply for a child under 5; US citizenship not required.
items.referral: Submit an application or call the clinic.

items.name: All Roads
items.description: Housing support and assessment, with levels of care matched to individual need, and other resources and support with the goal of ending homelessness.
items.address: Boulder (Mon–Fri 9–3): 4869 Broadway, Boulder, CO 80304; Longmont (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 12–5): 804 S. Lincoln St; Longmont (Wed 12–5): 1335 Francis St.
items.referral: Walk in or call to begin.

items.name: Boulder County Housing Helpline
items.description: Online directory connecting individuals and families to the housing resource that best fits their needs.
items.eligibility: Boulder County residents with housing needs
items.referral: Use the resource directory on the website.

items.name: HOPE for Longmont
items.description: Emergency shelter when temperatures are 25 degrees or below, street outreach for basic needs and connection to services, short-term shelter and services, case management, support with long-term housing, and pop-up medical clinics.
items.address: Outreach Center: 804 S. Lincoln Street, Longmont, CO 80501
items.referral: The first step is coordinated entry to assess and connect to services; call to begin.

items.name: The Inn Between of Longmont
items.description: Time-limited, affordable transitional housing for people facing homelessness; fixed-income housing for elderly people or people with disabilities; and contracted housing for people with high barriers to housing.
items.eligibility: Earning 60% or less of Area Median Income; 18+; living, working, or attending school in SVVSD for at least 30 days; able to live independently
items.referral: Apply online.

items.name: A Precious Child
items.description: Basic needs, access to enrichment, school supplies, and holiday gifts for families at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level or in need of emergency assistance.
items.eligibility: Referral from a partner agency; living in Adams, Arapahoe, Broomfield, Boulder, Denver, Douglas, Jefferson, or Weld County; parent or caregiver of a child 18 or younger
items.referral: Get a referral from a partner agency, then call to schedule an appointment.

items.name: Boulder County Personal Finance Program
items.description: Personalized meetings on money management, financial planning, finding financial assistance, credit building, and financial literacy. Appointments by phone, video, or in person.
items.address: Boulder: 3460 Broadway; Longmont: 515 Coffman St.; Lafayette: 1755 S. Public Road
items.referral: Schedule on the website, email personalfinancial@bouldercounty.gov, or call (720) 564-2279.

items.name: Boulder County Head Start
items.description: Promotes school readiness for young children through educational, nutritional, health, social, and other services.
items.eligibility: Low-income families with children ages 3–5 in Boulder County
items.address: Boulder: 2675 Mapleton Ave., Boulder, CO 80304 and 2850 Mapleton Ave., Boulder, CO 80301; Lafayette: 2802 Dagny Way, Lafayette, CO 80026
items.referral: Fill out the online application to see if your child qualifies.

items.name: A Woman's Work
items.description: A funding source for women in communities served by the St. Vrain Valley School District and the Town of Berthoud who need financial support for immediate needs that cannot be met by other sources.
items.referral: A referral must be made by a professional partner or a donor.

items.name: Benefits in Action
items.description: Help figuring out benefits such as SNAP, Medicare, Medicaid, OmniSalud, and LEAP.
items.eligibility: Families and individuals who need help applying for benefits
items.address: 12157 W Cedar Dr, Suite 100, Lakewood, CO 80228
items.referral: Apply online or call.

items.name: Colorado Immigrant Justice Fund
items.description: Financial assistance for legal representation.
items.eligibility: Families in need of legal representation for immigration
items.referral: Use the contact form at https://www.coloradoimmigrantjusticefund.org/contact-us

items.name: El Centro de las Familias (The Family Center)
items.description: High-quality childcare and supportive services, with an emphasis on cultural attunement with the Latinx community.
items.eligibility: Childcare: 6 weeks to 5 years old; family support: families with young children
items.referral: Apply online or email info@thefamilycenterfc.org.

items.name: TLC Learning Center
items.description: Inclusive early childhood education and pediatric therapy center in Longmont, providing childcare to neurotypical and neurodivergent children side by side. Free and low-cost options for qualifying families.
items.referral: Schedule a tour by calling or submitting a form online.

items.name: El Centro Amistad
items.description: Latine community organization; also offers counseling (individual services and a DBT parent group).
items.address: Boulder: 2338 Broadway, Boulder, CO 80304; Longmont: 1243 Sherman Dr., Suites 100D–100E, Longmont, CO 80501

items.name: Intercambio Uniting Communities
items.description: Resources for adult English language learners (ESL).
items.address: Boulder: 4735 Walnut St, Suite B, Boulder, CO 80301; Longmont: 1715 Iron Horse Dr., Suite 130, Longmont, CO 80501

items.name: Imagine!
items.category: Affinity Groups / Organizations: Disability; Family Support
items.description: Supports for people with developmental disabilities and their families.

items.name: BRITE Collaborative
items.description: Restorative justice.

items.name: Rocky Mountain Legal Center
items.description: Free and low-cost civil legal representation for low-income families, single parents, seniors, and people from all walks of life.

items.name: Longmont Library
items.notes: Conference rooms are the most private. Study rooms: check in for the reservation with staff on the 2nd floor within 15 minutes of the start time.

items.name: Broomfield Library
items.notes: The name on the reservation must match the patron using the room.

items.name: Boulder Library (Main)
items.notes: Study rooms: up to 2 hours per day, up to 3 weeks in advance. Meeting rooms: up to 16 hours per month, up to 16 weeks in advance.

items.name: George Reynolds Branch Library
items.notes: Study rooms: up to 2 hours per day, up to 3 weeks in advance. Meeting rooms: up to 16 hours per month, up to 16 weeks in advance.

items.name: Gunbarrel Library
items.notes: Study rooms: up to 2 hours per day, up to 3 weeks in advance. Meeting rooms: up to 16 hours per month, up to 16 weeks in advance.

items.name: Meadows Branch Library
items.notes: Study rooms: up to 2 hours per day, up to 3 weeks in advance. Meeting rooms: up to 16 hours per month, up to 16 weeks in advance.

items.name: NoBo Library
items.notes: Study rooms: up to 2 hours per day, up to 3 weeks in advance. Meeting rooms: up to 16 hours per month, up to 16 weeks in advance.

items.name: Broomfield Community Center
items.notes: Burns Room or one section of Elmwood. Once an organization account is created, as a nonprofit Rise will receive resident rates.

items.name: Carbon Valley Library
items.notes: Meeting Room 2 or the Collaboration Room.

items.name: Erie Community Center
items.referral: Complete the rental request form; response within 3 business days.
